messages:
maria_g: quick sync – want to lock down methodology for head-to-head model runs. goal: truly matched decode (same prompt, stop seq, tokenizer alignment) and isolate kernel/batching effects. suggestions?

devon: +1. biggest leaky variables we've seen: tokenizer detokenization differences, kv cache warm vs cold, and runtime kernel choice (fp16 vs int8 paths).

alex: agree. propose checklist per run:
- same prompt bytes (canonicalized whitespace)
- identical decode params (temp, top_k, stop tokens)
- force same tokenizer model and seed for sampling
- run cold vs warm KV cache variants
- collect kernel-selection trace + batch size histogram

sanjay: can we make the harness enforce tokenizer alignment? last time some models used byte-level differences and we lost 10-20ms due to re-tokenization.

maria_g: yes — harness should ship the tokenized inputs and the expected stop-token ids. replay should feed token ids directly when possible. sample config I'm thinking:

```
run_config = {
  \"prompt_file\": \"canonical_prompts.jsonl\",
  \"token_mode\": \"pretokenized\",   # options: raw, pretokenized
  \"decode\": {\"temp\": 0.0, \"top_k\": 40, \"stop_ids\": [50256]},
  \"kv_warm_steps\": [0, 1],
  \"batch_sizes\": [1, 4, 8]
}
```

rachel: runtime-bot: can we tag runs so kernel selection is deterministic? otherwise the runtime will pick the fastest kernel and we'll be comparing different code paths.

runtime-bot: kernel-tagging available. Use header: X-Kernel-Force: <kernel_name> or set ENV RUNTIME_KERNEL_HINT to one of [fast_attn_fp16, stable_int8, fallback_cuda].

devon: good — we'll do two passes per model: (A) force the same kernel across models; (B) allow runtime autotune and capture selection. Compare both.

alex: stats we need to capture per-request: latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, kernel_used, batch_fill, kv_hit_ratio, cpu_profile (hot funcs), nvprof summary.

sanjay: for KV warm/cold: make cold = new process per request (no persisted KV), warm = same session with primed prefix. That will replicate real-world chat scenarios.

maria_g: about synthetic vs replay traffic: replay wins for tokenizer alignment and real inter-token spacing. synthetic helps stress steady-state batch behavior. we should include both but don't mix results.

rachel: also add a micro-benchmark: single-step decode for kernel decode cost. small harness:
```
./micro_decode --model vX --tokens 1 --kernel fast_attn_fp16 --iters 1000
```

devon: turned on profiler and saw a regression on stable_int8 path: decode kernel had +12% cycles after last change. patch candidate: kernel fusing change. I'll attach flame snippet to the ticket.

alex: let's ensure run naming: <model>-<kernel>-<batch>-<kv>-<seed>.json so results map cleanly. example: gpt-madeup-stable_int8-b4-kvwarm-s42.json

sanjay: for apples-to-apples: we also need identical stop-seq handling. some models emit EOS id, others use user-supplied stop token. unify by post-processing to truncate on first match of stop_id sequence.

maria_g: final ask: QA — run 3 models tomorrow (open-v1, open-v2-quant, open-v2-fp16) across kernels and batch sizes. devon/alex to own harness changes; sanjay to validate tokenizer pretokenized outputs; rachel to wire kernel forcing in CI. I'll message infra to reserve GPUs.

devon: noted. will open PR with harness changes and example canonical_prompts.jsonl. :thumbsup: 

alex: adding a small regression test: replay a single session, compare token outputs (ids) between models and fail if mismatch length or stop positions differ. keeps apples strict.

rachel: quick FYI link to existing docs: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/benchmarking-token-protocol — will add a section on kernel forcing.

maria_g: thanks — if no blockers I'll kick off runs tomorrow 09:00 PT. :rocket:
